newsitem.title: FRANCE: Donor nations pledge $860 mln to Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Donor nations pledge $860 mln to Sri Lanka.

text.p: Donor nations on Monday pledged about $860 million to Sri Lanka for 1997, the World Bank said after a meeting in Paris.
The amount was a slight increase from the $850 million pledged in April 1995.
A statement from the Bank said disbursement of the sum, which it called "generous" would need improved project implementation methods.
The bank said the highest priority for Sri Lanka was peace and said donors were prepared to offer more aid if a settlement to end the island's civil war were reached.
"Deploring the cost of the hostilities and human suffering (donors) hoped that negotiations leading to a peaceful settlement could be initiated without delay," the bank said.
Donors also stressed the need for quicker structural reforms to the Sri Lankan economy and reduction of the fiscal deficit.
Public administration reform was also cited as a high priority, both to reduce the cost of the civil service and to make goverment more responsive to the needs of a modern economy.
It said these actions would promote private sector-led growth and employment.
